Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. - fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

Report findings concisely with exact file:line citations.

## 1. Memo lifecycle events that dispatch webhooks

| Event (`ActivityType`) | Trigger |
|---|---|
| `memos.memo.created` | Memo created |
| `memos.memo.updated` | Memo updated (also fired for attachment changes, relation changes — there is no separate "archived" event; archiving is a state field change that flows through the update path) |
| `memos.memo.deleted` | Memo deleted |
| `memos.memo.comment.created` | Comment created on a memo (notifies the related memo's owner) |

There is no dedicated `memo.archived` event — archive/unarchive goes through the regular update flow and fires `memos.memo.updated`.

## 2. Dispatch functions (file:line)

All in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`:

- `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` — `memo_service_webhooks.go:15` → calls `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook(ctx, memo, "memos.memo.created")`
- `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` — `memo_service_webhooks.go:20` → `"memos.memo.updated"`
- `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` — `memo_service_webhooks.go:25` → `"memos.memo.deleted"`
- `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` — `memo_service_webhooks.go:30` → sets `"memos.memo.comment.created"` directly and calls `webhook.PostAsync` itself (doesn't go through `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`)

Callers (where each is triggered in the RPC handlers):
- `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` called from `CreateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:157`
- `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` called from `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go:67`, which itself is called from:
  - `UpdateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:513`
  - `memo_attachment_service.go:48`
  - `memo_relation_service.go:48`
- `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` called from `DeleteMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:562`
- `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` called from `CreateMemoComment` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:119`

## 3. Convergence point (shared delivery function)

All roads lead to `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` at `memo_service_webhooks.go:48` (shared by created/updated/deleted; comment-created bypasses it but follows the identical pattern inline). This builds a `webhook.WebhookRequestPayload` via `convertMemoToWebhookPayload` (`memo_service_webhooks.go:76`) and hands off to:

**`webhook.PostAsync`** — `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`
This enqueues the payload onto a bounded channel (`asyncPostQueue`, 128 slots) consumed by 4 worker goroutines started in `init()` (`webhook.go:42-55`), each of which calls the actual synchronous HTTP delivery function:

**`webhook.Post`** — `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`
This is the true single point of convergence that performs the HTTP POST — it marshals the JSON body, builds the `http.Request`, optionally HMAC-signs it (Standard Webhooks style, `webhook-id`/`webhook-timestamp`/`webhook-signature` headers), and sends it via the shared `safeClient` (an `http.Client` with an SSRF-guarding `DialContext`, `webhook.go:32-37`).

So the chain is: `DispatchMemo{Created,Updated,Deleted}Webhook` → `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (memo_service_webhooks.go:48) → `webhook.PostAsync` (webhook.go:184) → async queue → `webhook.Post` (webhook.go:120, does the actual HTTP POST).</result>
